info.title: Off-Nadir Delta API
info.description: Query geolocated world event signals (Delta Signals), what changed about them, satellite imagery and collection planning, the Watchlist, and the World Brief. Authenticate with an API key (Authorization: Bearer ond_… or X-API-Key). Available on every plan; what a call returns follows the key owner's plan, and metered calls spend its token balance. The MCP server at POST /api/v1/mcp serves the conversational subset as tools; for a ChatGPT custom GPT, import /api/v1/openapi-gpt-actions.json.

get.description: Costs 3 token(s) per request. Supports cursor pagination via meta.next_cursor: follow it until it is null to read every matching signal (meta.total_count is exact — there is no cap on how many you can page through; each page is charged). meta.coverage reports what the bbox holds relative to the corpus (and how many signals exist worldwide for the same window), so an empty or thin result can be told apart from a quiet world. Plan-dependent: on a plan without the full event detail (Free) the reported facts beyond the casualty counts are withheld, and each of the collection reasoning (with the GEOINT score), the market reasoning, the full source list and the relations opens on its own per plan; `plan_lock` names what was withheld and `plan_lock.section_plans` the plan that opens each part — a null there means not shown, not unknown (the same rule as the app and the public event pages). The filters are the app's — the Watchfloor's and the Map's Signals panel, which are the same (date range or time window, search, category, stage, severity, publishers, market, location, sort) — with the same choices and the same rules; nothing the app does not offer is accepted, and a retired parameter is refused with its replacement named. Filters beyond category on the Watchfloor — q, stages, min_severity_band, min_publishers, markets and placement — need a plan with event filters (not Free), and linked_to and sort=geoint each need a plan that includes them; without them they are not applied and `meta.filter_clamp` lists the ones dropped, with `required_plans` naming the plan that opens each.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Bounding box "minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat" (WGS84). Omit for worldwide.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Date range start, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC) — the Watchfloor date range. Give with end_date, or neither for the recent window. The event record starts on 2026-09-23: a range before that date returns no events because none were recorded, not because none happened. The range is bounded by the key owner's plan — without real-time it ends yesterday, without the date range it ends on the latest readable day, and it never starts before the plan's history floor; meta.window_clamp says what was narrowed.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Date range end, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), inclusive.

parameters.name: recency
parameters.description: The Watchfloor time window: last reported in the last 15 min / hour / 24 hours. Default 24h when no date range is given. 15m and 1h need real-time; without it the 24 hours to the end of the latest readable day are used and meta.filter_clamp says so.

parameters.name: categories
parameters.description: Comma-separated category filter — the Watchfloor Category. Omit for all. Six categories are events made from a measurement or an official record, not from reporting: thermal_anomaly (heat sources measured by satellite), transit_anomaly (ship transits or port calls off their own recent level), nightlight_anomaly (night lights over a city below half of its own usual level), so2_anomaly (sulfur dioxide above background around a volcano with an ash advisory), quake_exposure (an earthquake with registered facilities within a set distance — distances, not shaking or damage) and cyclone_exposure (registered places inside the forecast tropical-storm-force wind radii of an Atlantic or eastern Pacific cyclone — a forecast, not an observation). They carry measured=true and measured_kind, state what was recorded and never a cause.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The Watchfloor search: title, summary, place, country and category. Every word must match; "two words" keeps the order; -word excludes. At most 300 characters.

parameters.name: stages
parameters.description: Comma-separated location stages (reported, localized, pinpointed): reported = country or province only, localized = town or city, pinpointed = street block or facility.

parameters.name: min_severity_band
parameters.description: The Watchfloor Severity filter: severity_band at least this (4 / 6 / 9).

parameters.name: min_publishers
parameters.description: The Watchfloor Publishers reporting filter (2 / 3 / 5). Breadth of reporting, not independent confirmation.

parameters.name: markets
parameters.description: Comma-separated market-impact filter (oil, natural_gas, grain, shipping, defense, metals, semiconductors, fx, equities): only signals AI-tagged as exposing these markets via a direct physical/supply channel. Informational only — not investment advice. Omit for all.

parameters.name: placement
parameters.description: The Watchfloor Location filter: all (default), map (precise enough to draw as a point) or list (placed only to a country or province). With a bbox, `signals` holds only events with a point inside it; events without a point whose country overlaps the bbox come separately in `country_level_signals` (the first 10, counted in meta.country_level) — placement=list returns all of those, paged. Without a bbox, list and all cover the whole world.

parameters.name: linked_to
parameters.description: The Watchfloor "Filter to these events" on a connector: only events that share it. One stored connector the events share: facility:<entity_id> (from search_entities or get_related_events), place:<place_key> (from get_related_events) or actor:<name> (a name in a signal's actors, case-insensitive). Needs a plan that includes it (meta.filter_clamp.required_plans names the plan when it is dropped).

parameters.name: watch_id
parameters.description: The Watchfloor "Near my places" for one place: only events linked to this watch (id from GET /api/v1/watches) — the same up-to-100 most recent events the Watchlist shows for that place, area or event. Another account’s watch, or an unknown id, is 404. meta.watch_linked_events says how many events the watch links; the other filters and the window still apply.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The Watchfloor Sort: latest (default), oldest, or geoint (Imaging value: a satellite could see it first, then the GEOINT score, then how finely the place is known). geoint, like the GEOINT score itself, needs a plan that includes it; without it latest is used and meta.filter_clamp says so.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Differential fetch: only signals refolded at/after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Narrows the window rather than replacing it; signals carry last_updated_at.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max rows per page (1-500, default 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from meta.next_cursor. Bound to the query it came from.

200.description: A page of signals.

country_level_signals.description: With a bbox: events that cannot be placed as a point (reported only to a country or province) whose country overlaps the bbox — not shown to be inside it. The first 10; meta.country_level counts them. Empty without a bbox.

get.summary: Fetch a single signal by id
get.description: Costs 1 token(s) per request. Returns exactly one signal by its id (the `id` from a signals result). An id that has since been folded into another event resolves to that event, and `meta.merged_from_request` says so. Plan-dependent: on a plan without the full event detail (Free) the reported facts beyond the casualty counts are withheld, and each of the collection reasoning (with the GEOINT score), the market reasoning, the full source list and the relations opens on its own per plan; `plan_lock` names what was withheld and `plan_lock.section_plans` the plan that opens each part — a null there means not shown, not unknown (the same rule as the app and the public event pages).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The signal id (UUID) from a /api/v1/signals result.

200.description: The signal.

get.description: Costs 2 token(s) per request. Returns a minimal metadata projection of matching STAC scenes (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, NISAR L-band) — no imagery bytes, no signed URLs. bbox is required.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Bounding box "minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat" (WGS84). Required.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: Catalog collection. Defaults to sentinel-2-l2a.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Date range start (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) — the app's imagery date range. Give with end_date, or neither for the last 7 days. At most 30 days.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Date range end (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC), inclusive.

parameters.name: event_date
parameters.description: Event date YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). When set, each scene is tagged timing=pre/post/same_day_unknown, the window is widened to the canonical pre/post span, and meta reports has_pre_baseline / has_post / bracketing_available / window_status; for sentinel-1-grd it also reports sar_pair_status + orbit_note.

parameters.name: event_point
parameters.description: Event point "lon,lat" (WGS84). When set, each scene reports target_relation (covers_event_geometry = geometry gate; usable_for_analysis additionally requires acceptable cloud for optical) so a scene that only clips the wide bbox — or a cloud-obscured optical scene — is not presented as usable for the event.

parameters.name: event_aoi
parameters.description: Event AOI bbox "minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat" (WGS84) for target_relation.intersects_event_aoi / event_aoi_coverage_ratio.

parameters.name: event_timestamp
parameters.description: Full event timestamp (ISO 8601) when known — promotes same-day scenes from same_day_unknown to pre/post by time.

parameters.name: cloud_cover_max
parameters.description: Sentinel-2 only: max cloud cover percentage.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max scenes to return.

200.description: Matching scenes (minimal metadata).

get.summary: Deterministic imagery plan for one event
get.description: Costs 4 token(s) per request (it deliberately issues two catalog searches). The SERVER decides which collections to search for the stated goal — sentinel-1-grd (SAR: all-weather, survives cloud and night) and sentinel-2-l2a (optical) exactly once each — against the event's own footprint and a pre/post window around its date, so the all-weather look can never be silently skipped and the same search is never repeated. Per search it reports why it was made, scenes returned, how many actually COVER the event and are usable (cloud-obscured optical does not count), the SAR pair status and whether a pre/post bracket exists, plus screening / detection / identification capability — a VHR recommendation never invalidates what the free catalog already showed. The vhr_recommendation.assessed flag says whether the VHR question was DECIDED at all: when the subject has no recorded ground-sampling requirement it comes back false, and recommended:false then means "not determined", NOT "not needed". An event with no resolvable footprint is refused rather than planned against a guess.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The signal id (UUID) from /api/v1/signals. An id folded into another event resolves to that event; meta.merged_from_request says so.

parameters.name: analysis_goal
parameters.description: damage_assessment | flood_mapping | wildfire_assessment.

parameters.name: event_date
parameters.description: Event date YYYY-MM-DD. Optional — the event row supplies it when known.

200.description: The executed plan, one step per collection.

get.description: Costs 1 token(s) per request. Crosses each event's composite IMPORTANCE (severity × source breadth × market relevance) with the SPEC CLASS its required resolution demands — coarse (≤100 m), hr (≤10 m, Sentinel-class free data) or vhr (sub-metre, commercial tasking) — and returns per-class counts with mean importance plus the top targets. Use it to triage before spending: a high-importance event needing only hr is answerable with free Sentinel data, while a vhr one is what a paid order is for. Deterministic; no LLM.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Area as "west,south,east,north" (WGS84). Omit for a global survey.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Inclusive start date YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today. Clamped to your plan history floor (and to yesterday without real-time); meta.window_clamp says what was narrowed. The event record starts on 2026-09-23: an earlier window returns no events because none were recorded, not because none happened.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Inclusive end date YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today. Window capped at 30 days.

parameters.name: categories
parameters.description: Comma-separated Delta categories to restrict to.

parameters.name: min_geoint_score
parameters.description: Drop events below this GEOINT score before ranking.

parameters.name: top_n
parameters.description: How many top targets to return (1..50, default 12).

200.description: Per-spec-class demand and the top collection targets.

get.summary: Exhaustive observability survey for a sensor
get.description: Costs 1 token(s) per request. Evaluates EVERY event in the window against a sensor's resolving power using each event's precomputed required resolution, and returns observable vs not counts, the breakdown by required resolution, and the top observable events with their imaging rationale. Observability is resolvability — whether the physical mark is large enough: sentinel-2 is ~10 m optical (needs daylight and clear sky), sentinel-1 is SAR (all-weather, day or night). Deterministic; no LLM and no per-event cost.

parameters.name: sensor
parameters.description: sentinel-2 (~10 m optical) or sentinel-1 (SAR). Default sentinel-2.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Area as "west,south,east,north" (WGS84). Omit for a global survey.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Inclusive start date YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today. Clamped to your plan history floor (and to yesterday without real-time); meta.window_clamp says what was narrowed. The event record starts on 2026-09-23: an earlier window returns no events because none were recorded, not because none happened.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Inclusive end date YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today. Window capped at 30 days.

parameters.name: categories
parameters.description: Comma-separated Delta categories to restrict to.

parameters.name: min_geoint_score
parameters.description: Drop events below this GEOINT score before surveying.

parameters.name: top_n
parameters.description: How many observable events to return (1..50, default 20).

200.description: Observable vs not, with the per-resolution breakdown.

get.summary: Next satellite passes over a target
get.description: Costs 2 token(s) per request. Propagates current orbital elements (SGP4 over day-cached CelesTrak two-line elements) and returns the access windows over a point for 13 families: Sentinel-1 (SAR), Sentinel-2, Landsat and NISAR are free and SYSTEMATIC (routinely collecting sensors — each pass is still a geometric opportunity, not a scheduled acquisition; units whose operator announced the end of operations are excluded); WorldView, ICEYE, Capella, SkySat, Umbra, Synspective, iQPS, RADARSAT-2 and COSMO-SkyMed are commercial and AGILE (taskable ACCESS opportunities that require a paid order — NOT guaranteed collects). Each pass carries acquisition/loss and closest-approach times, peak elevation, off-nadir angle, ground distance, ascending/descending, solar elevation and sunlit flag, plus the age of the element set used. Give lat and lon, or a bbox whose centre is used. The window is capped to a 7-day horizon. When orbital elements cannot be retrieved the response sets retrieval_ok:false — that means timing is UNAVAILABLE, never "no passes". Orbital data by CelesTrak.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Target latitude (-90..90; positive = North). Required unless bbox is given.

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Target longitude (-180..180; positive = East). Required unless bbox is given.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Area as "west,south,east,north" (WGS84). The CENTRE is used as the target when lat/lon are omitted.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Inclusive start date YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). Defaults to today.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Inclusive end date YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). Defaults to start+2 days; capped to a 7-day horizon.

parameters.name: satellites
parameters.description: Comma-separated family keys to consider: sentinel-1, sentinel-2, landsat, nisar, worldview, iceye, capella, skysat, umbra, synspective, iqps, radarsat-2, cosmo-skymed. Omit for all thirteen.

parameters.name: max_passes
parameters.description: Maximum passes to return, soonest first (1..100, default 40).

200.description: Access windows over the target, soonest first.

collection_mode.description: systematic = a routinely collecting sensor (a geometric opportunity, not a scheduled acquisition); agile = a taskable access opportunity requiring a paid order.

off_nadir_deg.description: 0 = overhead. Large angles degrade resolution and geometry.

solar_elevation_deg.description: At the target, at peak. Below 0 = night.

sunlit.description: Optical needs light; SAR does not.

tle_age_days.description: Days between the element-set epoch and THIS pass. Signed: negative means the pass precedes the epoch (a hindcast), not that the elements are from the future.

stale.description: Elements older than 7 days — predicted timing may drift by minutes.

retrieval_ok.description: false = orbital elements could not be retrieved; timing is unavailable, NOT "no passes".

get.summary: What changed about the events in an area
get.description: Metered like /signals. Returns CHANGES rather than rows: polling /signals and diffing the ids finds new REPORTING, which is a different thing — a 2025 attack re-reported in 2026 with a fresh attribution is indistinguishable from a fresh attack. Each development says which `axis` moved, what the value was and what it became, what the change rests on (`basis`), and is labelled `world` (the event’s own state moved: a death toll revised, a perpetrator named) or `measurement` (what we can now see moved: a location resolved, the evidence stage advanced). The window filters on WHEN THE CHANGE WAS OBSERVED, so a change to an older event is returned. Default returns only changes worth a person’s attention; notable_only=false returns the full ledger. Plan-dependent: on a plan without the full event detail (Free), every change keeps its time and axis, but only each event’s latest change keeps its value (never for the reported facts — attribution, means, targets, target status); with the full detail, every change keeps its value. Changes to post-event imagery are not returned here: imagery is checked only for events on the Watchlist, and a watch carries its own imagery state. Only a plan that includes the sources keeps the sources behind each change. locked_by says when a value was withheld, and sources_locked says when only the sources were.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat. Omit for worldwide.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Date range start (YYYY-MM-DD) — the app's date range. Give with end_date, or neither for today. Changes are recorded from 2026-09-23, when the event record starts. The plan's history window bounds it.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Date range end (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive.

parameters.name: categories
parameters.description: Comma-separated signal categories.

parameters.name: axes
parameters.description: Comma-separated change axes (casualties_killed, attributed_actor, stage, location_level, ...). An unknown value is a 400, never an empty result — a silent zero reads as "nothing happened".

parameters.name: notable_only
parameters.description: Default true. False returns every recorded change, including minor ones.

parameters.name: include_member_count
parameters.description: Default false. The member_count axis means "one more report arrived", which says nothing new about the event — including it puts every followed-up story in today’s changes.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many developments to return (1..200, default 50).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Skip this many developments (meta.total_count is the whole window).

200.description: Developments, newest first, with the canonical event each belongs to.

get.description: Free. The full history of a single event: its current state, every change in the order it happened, and every source behind it grouped by outlet. Answers "is this a new event or an update to an old one". occurred_at is when the event HAPPENED, and occurred_at_basis says whether that was stated in a report, absent from it, or never measured — three different things that a single null would hide. timeline_total is the number of recorded changes (the array is capped), and timeline_note says why an empty timeline is not an absence of knowledge. Plan-dependent: changes before the key owner's history window keep their time and axis but not their values. On a plan without the full event detail (Free), only the latest change keeps its value (never for withheld facts); with it, every change keeps its value unless its section is withheld. Without the sources no change keeps its sources, the source list keeps only each outlet's latest report and each fact loses the report it came from; the related events and the imaging recommendation are withheld unless the plan includes them — locked_by says why a value was withheld, sources_locked says when only the sources were, and plan_lock names what was withheld with section_plans naming the plan that opens each part.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event id (UUID). An id folded into another event resolves to that event, and merged_from_request says so.

200.description: The canonical event, its timeline, and its sources.

get.description: Free. Lists the named map configurations saved on this account, most recently changed first, with layer count, size, tags and timestamps. The serialized layer tree is not returned — it is an internal representation, not a public contract.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max layer sets to return.

200.description: Your saved layer sets.

get.description: Free. Reads one saved map configuration by id — one this account owns, a public one, or one shared with it (the same rule as the app). Returns 404 when there is no layer set with that id that this account can open. `contents` is always "not_exposed": the serialized layer tree is internal.

parameters.name: layerSetId
parameters.description: The layer set id.

200.description: The layer set.

get.description: Free. Lists the data uploaded to the map on this account, newest first, and the formats the uploader accepts. Uploading itself is a multipart file transfer in the app, not a JSON call, so it has no endpoint here.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max uploads to return.

200.description: Your uploaded layers and the accepted formats.

get.description: Free. Lists the standing orders on this key with each one’s cadence, watched area, last check, last fire, and quiet_checks (consecutive checks that found nothing). Also returns how many orders your plan allows and how many remain.

200.description: Your standing orders and the plan limits that apply to them.

min_interval_hours.description: 24 = daily allowed, 168 = weekly is the fastest.

post.description: Free to create. The app’s "Watch this area": saves a bounding box and checks it weekly for new events, notifying only when something crossed the reporting bar. The question, cadence, categories and thresholds are not accepted (the app does not offer them); passing them returns 400. Checks are deterministic: when new events cross the bar you receive a digest of them, and no model is run and nothing is charged, whether or not anything was found. The order count is plan-gated; a 403 says which limit you hit.

bbox.description: Area to watch, [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] (WGS84). Required, and at most 100,000 km² — a larger box returns 400 invalid_input (to follow a whole country, create a watch with target_type "site" and scale "country").

notify_email.description: Email the result when it fires (default true). Results are readable from the list either way.

201.description: The created standing order and the watch it appears under.

403.description: You are at your plan’s order limit.

get.description: Free. Lists the places under continuous satellite measurement on this key, with each area’s metric, latest value, change since the previous measurement, anomaly flag, and coverage. Coverage window_total is null when the catalog total is unknown — null is not zero. The measurement history itself is on GET /api/v1/monitoring/{areaId}.

200.description: Your monitored areas, the plan limits that apply, and how metering works.

post.description: Free to create. Fixes a bounding box and a quantity to measure; every new acquisition over it is measured automatically from then on. Each automatic check costs 2 tokens plus 0.5 per new scene measured, and a check that finds no new acquisition costs nothing. The area must be under 5,000 km² and the sensor is chosen from the metric. Requires the monitoring plan feature; area count is plan-gated and a 403 says which limit you hit.

bbox.description: Area to measure, [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] (WGS84). Must be under 5,000 km².

metric.description: What to count. Plain words work (ships, fires, vegetation, water, burn, snow, built_up, moisture, night_lights) as do index names (ship_detection, fire_count, ndvi, evi, savi, ndmi, ndwi, mndwi, ndbi, ndsi, nbr, dnb, vv, vh, rvi, rfdi, cr).

satellite.description: The sensor to measure with, chosen the way the app’s monitoring form does it (satellite × metric) — e.g. ship detection on Sentinel-1 or on NISAR. Omit for the metric’s first sensor (ship detection: Sentinel-1).

start_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD to begin the history from (default 3 months ago, as in the app). A longer backfill measures more scenes and costs more on the first check.

201.description: The created area, and how it will be metered.

403.description: Your plan does not include monitoring, or you are at the area limit.

get.summary: Get a monitored area and its measurement history
get.description: Free, and needs a plan that includes data export (otherwise 403 forbidden, with `denial` naming the plan that opens it). Returns one area with the full time series for every metric on it — each measured acquisition, its value, and whether it was flagged anomalous. Anomaly flags come from a median-absolute-deviation test on the series, not a fixed threshold. A metric’s polygon_id is accepted here as well as the area_id.

parameters.name: areaId
parameters.description: The area_id from the list endpoint (a metric polygon_id also resolves).

200.description: The area with its full measurement history.

404.description: No monitored area with that id on this key.

get.summary: Thermal anomalies: heat sources measured by satellite
get.description: Costs 3 token(s) per request — the same as a page of signals, and the same plan window applies (meta.window_clamp says when it was cut). A thermal anomaly is a satellite measurement, not a report (fire radiative power, VIIRS on NOAA-20 / NOAA-21 / Suomi NPP via NASA FIRMS). Two kinds are returned. kind=facility: a heat source of at least 10 MW within 2 km of a registered facility — a refinery, power plant, port, base, dam, bridge and the like; airports are excluded — that is at least 5 times the strongest detection within 500 m of the same spot in the 21 days before (or where none was detected). kind=night_source: a night-time heat source of at least 20 MW with no registered facility within 2 km, at least 5 times its own spot's 21-day maximum and 3 times that of the surrounding 10 km, compact and with little burning around it; its facility and distance_m are null, and it does not rule out vegetation fires. Each record states what was measured — strength, time, satellite, the earlier level, and for kind=facility the distance to the facility — and never a cause: a detection does not distinguish an attack, an accident, flaring or a vegetation fire, and the heat source may be outside the facility. Every record is also an event (same event_id as GET /api/v1/signals with categories=thermal_anomaly, where it carries measured=true and measured_kind=thermal), so the event endpoints work on it. linked_events lists reported events tied to the same facility by name within 3 days of the detection; it needs a plan with event relations (otherwise null, and meta.notes says so). Severity is inherited from linked reporting and is null when there is none. The measurement detail — which facility or place it was near, the distance, the strength, the summary and linked_events — needs a plan with the full event detail. Without it every record still returns that a heat source was measured, when, the pixel position and its kind, with detail_withheld=true, a placeholder title and null in the withheld fields (meta.detail_included and meta.detail_required_plan say so); the same records in GET /api/v1/signals carry the placeholder title too. Cursor pagination via meta.next_cursor.

get.summary: Transit anomalies: ship transits at straits and canals against their usual level
get.description: Costs 3 token(s) per request — the same as a page of signals. Takes no parameters: every strait and canal where ship transits are measured (28 places — Hormuz, Suez, Bab el-Mandeb, Malacca, Bosporus, Panama, Taiwan Strait and others) is returned in one response, the places outside their usual range first. A transit anomaly is a measurement, not a report. Each place carries status — usual, below or above its usual range, or not_measured — and level, an index computed by this product: the 7-day average of ship transits with the usual level set to 100 (index), the change against usual (change, 0.05 = +5%), the same index for tankers alone (tanker_index), and revised when the underlying figure changed after it was first recorded. Ship counts are not returned. Usual level: the median of the 7-day averages over the 12 weeks before. A 7-day average is outside its usual range when it is statistically unusual against those weeks (modified Z-score of 3.5 or more) and at least 15% away. meta.definition carries the same sentence. get.summary: Night-light anomalies: city night lights below half of their own usual level
get.description: Costs 3 token(s) per request — the same as a page of signals, and the same plan window applies (meta.window_clamp says when it was cut). A night is judged only when at least 70% of the city's box could be observed; the usual level is the median of the most recent earlier such nights (at least 5, at most 30). Nights of one continuing drop are one record (a new record starts after a judged night that was not a drop, or a gap of more than 3 days). Each record carries the city (name, country, centre and the half-size of its box), night (the latest night of the drop, a UTC date), first_night and nights (every drop night in the record), ratio_to_usual and percent_of_usual (0.41 / 41 = 41% of the usual level), observed_share (how much of the box was observed that night), baseline_nights, product (the Black Marble product, e.g. VJ146A2_NRT), granule (the product file the value was read from) and provisional. provisional=true means the value came from the near-real-time product and can change when the standard product arrives about nine days later. Where the plan includes the collection section, a watched event’s imagery is then checked automatically at 1 token a day per watch, until before and after scenes are found or 14 days after the first report; a day without enough tokens is skipped and not charged, and on other plans imagery is not checked and nothing is charged. target_type "event": pass the signal’s id (uuid) as event_id — the server resolves and binds the CANONICAL event (never an article URL), so further reporting and even a later cluster merge stay on the same watch. target_type "area": pass a bbox — created as a saved bookmark; to measure something there use POST /api/v1/monitoring, to watch its events use POST /api/v1/standing-orders (both join the same watch automatically). target_type "site": watch a specific place for change — a registry facility (entity_id from GET /api/v1/entities/search) or any point (lat, lon) — at a scale: "facility" (radius 250 m–3 km; measured from imagery by default when the kind of facility has a suggested measurement, e.g. vessel counts for a port), "city" (radius 5–20 km; measured only when you pass a metric) or "country" (followed through reporting only; never measured). The webhook URL itself is never returned. Connecting is done in the app (account settings → Chat notifications), because it goes through Slack’s or Discord’s own consent screen; which watches post there is `notify_chat` on each watch.

200.description: The connected channel (or null) and the providers that can be connected.

delete.description: Free. Removes the connected Slack or Discord channel; nothing is posted there afterwards. Watches keep their `notify_chat` setting, so connecting a channel again resumes posting for the same watches. 404 when none is connected.

200.description: Disconnected.

post.summary: Send a test message to your Slack / Discord channel
post.description: Free. Posts one short confirmation message to the connected channel and reports whether it was accepted. If the provider says the channel is gone, the connection is stopped (`disabled: true`) and has to be connected again in the app. 404 when none is connected; 400 when the connection was already stopped.

200.description: Whether the message was accepted.

get.description: Free. Terrain height from the Copernicus DEM GLO-30 at a point (lat+lon) or over an area (bbox): min, max, mean, median, p10, p90 and relief (max-minus-min). Use POST for a polygon, whose statistics cover only the samples inside the ring. A SURFACE model (buildings and canopy included), ~30 m posting, heights orthometric on EGM2008. Land only: no coverage over open ocean is reported as absence, never as 0 m. The response carries the required attribution; cite it wherever a height is shown.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude of a single point (use with lon).

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitude of a single point (use with lat).

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Area as "lon_min,lat_min,lon_max,lat_max" (WGS84).

200.description: Elevation measurement.

post.description: Free. Terrain height statistics over a drawn polygon, computed from the DEM samples INSIDE the ring rather than its bounding box — an L-shaped or diagonal AOI would otherwise report ground the caller never selected. Same model and caveats as GET /api/v1/elevation.

polygon.description: WGS84 ring [[lon, lat], …] with at least 3 vertices. A GeoJSON Polygon or Feature is also accepted.

bbox.description: Alternative to polygon: [lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max].

200.description: Elevation measurement over the polygon interior.

get.description: Free. Two computations derived from the Copernicus DEM GLO-30, both returned from a single read. `operation=sar_geometry` over a bbox, with `incidence_deg` and `look_azimuth_deg`, returns the share of the area lost to LAYOVER and SHADOW, the share merely foreshortened, and the mean local incidence angle — the arithmetic behind whether radar can actually use that ground, which changes with the pass direction and must not be assumed. `operation=profile` between two points returns the ground along the line and a LINE-OF-SIGHT verdict including Earth curvature: where the terrain first rises above the sight line, and by how much at worst. Both state the sample spacing they were computed at, because a coarser grid reads flatter and therefore more observable than the ground is. A SURFACE model, so canopy and buildings are included. Cite the returned attribution.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: Which computation to run.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: For sar_geometry: area as "lon_min,lat_min,lon_max,lat_max" (WGS84).

parameters.name: incidence_deg
parameters.description: For sar_geometry: sensor incidence angle. Sentinel-1 IW spans roughly 29-46 degrees.

parameters.name: look_azimuth_deg
parameters.description: For sar_geometry: compass bearing the sensor looks along the ground range. A right-looking descending pass looks roughly west (270).

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: For profile: latitude of the observer end.

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: For profile: longitude of the observer end.

parameters.name: to_lat
parameters.description: For profile: latitude of the far end.

parameters.name: to_lon
parameters.description: For profile: longitude of the far end.

parameters.name: observer_height_m
parameters.description: For profile: eye height above the ground, default 2 m. Use the real mast or tower height when that is the question.

200.description: The requested terrain computation.

post.summary: Spectral-index time series over an area
post.description: Measure a spectral index over a polygon, scene by scene, back through the Sentinel-2 archive — the answer to "how has this changed since <year>". Costs 0.5 tokens per scene ACTUALLY measured; a scene that fails to read appears in `skipped` and is not charged. Send `estimate_only: true` first: that is free and returns how many scenes match, the real date span, and what measuring them would cost. Three limits the response states rather than hides — the archive begins 2015-06-27 so an earlier start is clamped (`clamped_to_archive`), at most 24 scenes are measured per call so a longer period comes back as a sample with the rest in `skipped`, and `trend` compares the first and last measured scene only, so it is not a fitted rate. For a SAR quantity, or to keep measuring as new imagery arrives, create a monitored area instead.

polygon.description: WGS84 ring [[lon, lat], …] with at least 3 vertices. Statistics cover the samples INSIDE it. A GeoJSON Polygon or Feature is also accepted.

bbox.description: Alternative to polygon: [lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max] (WGS84).

index.description: Which optical index to measure: ndvi, evi, savi, ndmi, ndwi, mndwi, ndbi, ndsi, nbr, iron-oxide, clay, ferrous.

start.description: Start date YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). Clamped forward to 2015-06-27 if earlier.

max_scenes.description: Cap on scenes measured in this call. Server maximum 24.

max_cloud_cover.description: Scene cloud-cover ceiling in percent. Default 30.

estimate_only.description: True = free: return the scene count, date span and token cost WITHOUT measuring or charging.

200.description: The measured series, or the free estimate when estimate_only was set.

series.description: Present when a measurement ran: samples, skipped, trend, notes.

post.summary: Count vessels in a SAR scene
post.description: Count vessel-like targets in ONE Sentinel-1 or NISAR scene over an area, using CFAR detection. Costs 5 tokens per detection (a NISAR granule converted for the first time adds 1, and needs the plan's NISAR access); a scene the worker refuses (an unsupported combination, an area with no usable sea) is not charged. Get `item_id` from GET /api/v1/imagery first. **Read `caveats` before quoting the count**: it says when the land mask was unavailable (shoreline structures may be counted as vessels), how far from the coast detections were excluded (the default excludes vessels alongside a quay), and when the scene covers only part of the requested area — a partial-coverage count must not be compared with a full one as though the difference were vessels. This measures one scene at one time; to track a berth over time, create a monitored area with metric `ships`.

collection.description: Catalog collection of the scene: Sentinel-1, or NISAR L-band (the granule is converted to a COG first, which costs extra tokens the first time).

item_id.description: STAC item id of the scene, as returned by GET /api/v1/imagery.

bbox.description: Area to search within the scene, [lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max] (WGS84). Must be under 120,000 km².

geometry.description: Alternative to bbox: a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon.

algorithm_version.description: Detector version. 'auto' picks the recommended version for the sensor.

200.description: The detections, with the caveats that change what the count means.

processing.description: Algorithm version, configuration hash, land-mask source, sea ratio.

get.description: Free. Remaining token balance and plan capabilities for the calling key — pre-flight a metered call.

200.description: Usage snapshot.

get.description: Free. How current the data is (ingestion/enrichment frontier), the Daily World Brief status, and an Operational/Delayed/Degraded roll-up — pre-flight whether data is fresh before spending on a metered query.

200.description: Data freshness snapshot.

data_current_through.description: Ingestion frontier (newest slot ingested), ISO 8601 UTC.

services.description: Every component behind the answers, probed every 10 minutes. `components[]` carries one entry per surface with its status (operational | degraded | down | stale | unknown) and `owner` — "delta" for surfaces we run (public REST, MCP, the signal projection, metering, key auth, Watchlist measurements, report serving) and "provider" for upstream dependencies (STAC catalogs, tiles, auth, news search, NASA credentials). "stale" and "unknown" mean the probe itself has not confirmed recently, NOT that the service is fine. live_news_retrieval is kept as a named shortcut to the one check that had this block to itself.

components.description: One entry per monitored surface. Empty when the probe record could not be read — which is not the same as everything being healthy.

server.description: Server identity: version, negotiated protocol versions, live tool count and the three contract fingerprints (schema/description/descriptor hash) — the same block GET /api/v1/version returns.

get.description: Free and unauthenticated. Returns the live build identity — MCP server version, negotiated protocol versions, served tool count, and the schema / description / descriptor hashes — so an operator can confirm which build is live without holding an API key.

200.description: Server identity.

get.summary: Fetch the World Brief (daily, weekly or monthly)
get.description: Free of token charges. Returns the persisted AI-synthesized world brief. period=daily (default) is open on every plan for the days inside the key owner's plan history window (the same window as the app's Reports); an earlier date returns 403. Weekly and monthly are opened by the key owner's plan (the same entitlement as the app's Reports) and return 403 otherwise. Counts in stats cover every event in the window.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: daily (default), weekly or monthly.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). For daily, the day the brief covers; for weekly / monthly, the last day of the period (period_end — available_periods lists them). Defaults to the latest available.

200.description: The world brief for the requested (or latest) day or period.

period.description: weekly / monthly only: type, start, end.

available_periods.description: weekly / monthly only: recent published periods.

post.summary: AI RS deep-dive assessment for a signal
post.description: Costs 5 (quick) / 15 (deep) tokens. Available on every plan, including Free; metered on your token balance. A prior (event, kind) assessment is cached and not re-charged.

kind.description: Assessment depth. quick=5 tok, deep=15 tok. Defaults to quick.

200.description: Assessment result.

post.summary: Ask the Delta Analyst (agentic OSINT/GEOINT Q&A)
post.description: Costs 5–123 tokens, metered by the compute the question actually uses; the exact charge is returned in meta.tokens.charged (once, on completion). Follows the key owner's plan — whether Delta Agent is included and how many questions a month (a refusal is 403 with `denial` naming the plan that opens it) — and is metered on your token balance. Hybrid async: waits up to ~95s and returns the brief (200); a longer run returns 202 with a job_id — poll GET /api/v1/analyst/{jobId}, or re-send the SAME Idempotency-Key header to re-fetch the finished brief without a second charge. Timing: most questions finish in ~30–90s; a complex brief (satellite-imagery lookups or many sources) can take 2–3 minutes, so the 202 path is expected for those.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: At-most-once key. A re-send with the same key resolves to the SAME run: done → the brief (no re-charge); still running → 202 with the job_id.

bbox.description: Optional focus bounding box [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] (WGS84).

mode.description: fast (default) or deep. Deep enables extended reasoning and wider evidence-gathering budgets for forecasting, collection trade-offs and market-implication questions; it is slower and the ceiling rises from 123 to 415 tokens. Charging stays metered by what the run actually consumes.

200.description: Structured analyst brief (meta.tokens has the charge; meta.job_id identifies the run).

202.description: Run still in progress; finished in the background. Poll poll_url for the brief.

estimated_charge.description: The charge ceiling fixed for this run at enqueue; the completed job echoes it as meta.tokens.maximum_promised and never exceeds it.

get.summary: Poll an async Delta Analyst job
get.description: Free. Fetch the state (and, when done, the brief) of an analyst run started by POST /api/v1/analyst. Jobs are visible only to the API key owner that created them.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: The job_id returned by POST /api/v1/analyst.

200.description: Job state; brief, structured, result_quality, freshness and meta.tokens are present when status is done (same detail as MCP get_analyst_job).

progress.description: Pipeline progress while status is processing. completed_steps equals total_steps ONLY when the job is done.

structured.description: When done: the structured projection of the brief (claims with evidence classes, findings, citations, and the assembled structured_summary markdown). Same shape as MCP get_analyst_job.

result_quality.description: When done: the quality gates — status (complete|partial), schema_validation, semantic_validation, verification, deliverable_validation, repairs, issues.

freshness.description: When done: analysis_generated_at, evidence_cutoff_at, cache_age_seconds and freshness_status — a re-fetch returns a stored brief.

meta.description: When done: meta.tokens carries `charged` and `maximum_promised` (the ceiling fixed at enqueue).

Error.description: Error response with a stable machine-readable code.

denial.description: Present on a 403 when the key owner's plan refuses the request. Says which decision refused it, whether it is not included (plan_required) or a limit was reached (plan_limit), and the cheapest plan that opens it (null when none does).

coverage.description: What the requested bbox holds relative to the corpus. `global_available` is the number of signals worldwide for the SAME window and categories, counted through the same query — null when it was not established (not probed, probe failed, or more than the row cap exist, in which case `global_capped` is true). Response filters (markets, severity, observability, tasking gates) are applied per-row afterwards and are NOT applied to this count, so no count is offered when any of them is active.

bbox_area_share.description: Fraction of the world this bbox covers, by spherical area (1 = worldwide).

hints.description: Deterministic next steps implied by the numbers. Empty when none apply.

Signal.description: Stable public shape of a signal (additive changes only). 2026-09 corpus migration: the GDELT-era fields (goldstein_scale, avg_tone, num_mentions, integer ids) are gone — their inputs no longer exist — and the evidence ladder (stage / stage_reason) replaces the read-time observability derivations.

occurred_at.description: When the event happened, to the precision in occurred_at_precision. Null when reporting never said.

occurred_at_basis.description: What occurred_at rests on — stated in the reporting, or inferred.

last_reported_at.description: Most recent report. The start_date/end_date range filters on the UTC day of this field.

location_level.description: How precisely the place was resolved. lat/lng are rounded to match — a country-level fix is not reported to metre precision.

location_level_reported.description: What the reporting named, which can be coarser than what was resolved.

plottable.description: Whether the coordinate is precise enough to draw as a point. false means the fix is an area — do not render a pin, and do not task from it.

stage.description: How far the place is established: reported (country or province only, or not placeable) → localized (town or city) → pinpointed (street block or facility). Whether a satellite could see it is `collection.observable`; credibility is `reporting.credibility_best`.

stage_reason.description: Why the place is not established more precisely — e.g. a named facility not yet found on the map (it can be looked up) versus no report naming anything finer.

geoint_score.description: How much a satellite look would add.

impact_level.description: Delta Impact Scale: the highest public threshold the reported figures cross (0 not a physical event … 5 = 1,000 or more killed or 800,000 or more displaced). Worked out by fixed rules, not by a model; null when the reports give no casualty or damage figure. Our own scale — see /methodology/scales. severity_score beside it is an AI reading.

geoint_readiness.description: Delta GEOINT Readiness: whether satellite imagery can check the event, looked up from three recorded facts (A = checkable now with free imagery … E = not checkable from orbit). Part of the collection section: null on a plan without it. Our own table — see /methodology/scales.

means.description: How it was carried out, as reported.

target_effects.description: Condition of each named target a report describes individually (the latest report stating it). A site with no entry has no stated condition — not "undamaged". disputed = another report states a different condition. The source reports are on the event thread (canonical_event.targets).

attribution_basis.description: What the attribution rests on. An attribution resting on one party's claim says so here.

disputed.description: Reports disagree on the count. Not averaged — surfaced as a disagreement.

measured.description: true = made from a measurement or an official record, not from reporting (see measured_kind). Its reporting counts are 0.

measured_kind.description: thermal = a heat source measured by satellite (GET /api/v1/thermal-anomalies returns the measurement under the same id); transit = ship transits through a strait or canal that left their own recent level (GET /api/v1/transit-anomalies returns the level of every measured place and, for one outside its usual range, this event id); nightlight = night lights over a city that fell below half of the city's own usual level, measured by satellite — the cause is not established by the record (GET /api/v1/nightlight-anomalies returns the measurement under the same id, and the level of every monitored city); so2 = sulfur dioxide clearly above the local background around a volcano with a current volcanic ash advisory, measured by satellite — not the size of an eruption, and not whether ash was present (GET /api/v1/so2-anomalies returns the measurement under the same id); quake_exposure = an earthquake recorded by USGS within a set distance of registered facilities — a seismic record and distances; it does not measure shaking or damage at any facility (GET /api/v1/quake-exposures returns the facilities and distances under the same id); cyclone_exposure = registered facilities and straits inside the tropical-storm-force wind radii of a U.S. National Hurricane Center forecast advisory, now or within 48 hours — a forecast for the Atlantic, eastern Pacific and central Pacific, not an observation of wind or damage (GET /api/v1/cyclone-exposures returns the advisory and the places under the same id). null for events made from reporting.

occurrence_status.description: How far the event itself is established. claimed = the only party stating it is the side saying it carried it out. disputed = the side said to have been hit, or an authority, denies it. null = not yet assessed (NOT "confirmed"). Who claimed and who denied are on the event thread (canonical_event.occurrence).

member_count.description: Reports folded into this one event.

distinct_hosts.description: Distinct outlets among them. Syndication is not collapsed — breadth of carriage, not independence.

distinct_texts.description: Distinct texts among them: outlets carrying the same wire copy count once. Not a count of independent confirmations — different texts can rest on the same single statement. null = not yet counted.

collection.description: What a satellite could do about it.

gap.description: What stands in the way of a look (cloud, night, revisit).

observable.description: Whether a satellite could see it: the effect is large enough to show from orbit (observability) AND the place is established finely enough to frame it (0.3 m marks need a street block or facility). null = not assessed, which is not "no".

observability.description: NOT a probability: the coarsest resolution at which the effect still shows. 3 = visible at 10 m (flooding, burn scars), 2 = 3 m (several damaged buildings), 1 = 0.3 m (a single building), 0 = nothing shows from orbit. Higher means a coarser image suffices — lower means the location has to be known more precisely before anything can be pointed at it.

market_exposure.description: The evidence chain behind market_impact. basis="evidence_chain" means each tag carries its own evidence.

created_at.description: When this event was first opened. created_since filters on it.

last_updated_at.description: When it was last refolded. updated_since filters on it.

assessed_at.description: When the collection assessment last ran. Null means it has not run — not that nothing is observable.

plan_lock.description: What the key owner's plan withholds from this signal (null when nothing is). Without the full event detail the reported facts beyond casualty counts, and — each by its own plan — the collection reasoning, GEOINT score and market reasoning, are null here because they are not shown — not because they are unknown.

required_plan.description: The cheapest plan that opens the first withheld part (derived from the current plans; null when no plan does).

section_plans.description: For each withheld section, the cheapest plan that opens it — what happened (facts, places) opens before the evidence (sources, collection, markets, relations).
